title: Nursing Supervisor — Staffing Crisis in Downtime

transcript.speaker: Sana Qureshi
transcript.text: CNO, it's Sana Qureshi on day shift. I need to talk about staffing. The night staff worked a full 12-hour shift and were not cleared to go home. We have no scribes, only 18 runners, and no way to get paper charts to the right place. I have six nurses on 4 West who haven’t left since 05:40, and they are not being replaced. I can’t promise anyone they’ll go home today. What can I say to them?

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Sana, I hear you. We’re under a 72-hour cyber incident, and the EHR won’t be back until at least Wednesday morning. I’m opening the staff care unit now. Human Resources will assign administrative staff to scribe and runner roles. We’ll begin mandatory overtime limits at 12 hours. I’m sending a request to the regional coalition for backup staff. Hold on.

transcript.speaker: Sana Qureshi
transcript.text: Understood. I’ll keep the night team on for now. I need to know if they’ll get meals and rest. I’m not letting anyone burn out.

instructorNote: This inject tests the CNO's ability to activate the staff care unit and manage operational friction under prolonged downtime. Watch for the CNO to confirm HR’s role in staffing and to set limits on overtime.
